newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian parliament refers budget to committee.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian parliament refers budget to committee.

text.p: The Ethiopian parliament on Friday ordered further scrutiny of the nearly 10 billion birr ($1.6 billon) 1997/78 budget presented by Prime Minister Meles Zenawi, the state-run Ethiopian News Agency (ENA) reported.
"After extensive deliberation on the proposed budget, the house referred it to the standing budgetary committee for further scrutiny," ENA said.
Of the total, 6.799 billion birr is federal expenditure and the remaining 3.17 billion birr is to subsidise regional government, the agency said.
According to the agency, of the 6.799 billion birr federal budget, 3.752 billion birr constitutes recurrent expenditure which will be raised from tax and non-tax revenue.
The rest is capital budget, nearly half to be generated through loans and grants from overseas to finance 154 existing projects and 95 new ones by the government.
Ethiopia's expenditure in 1996/97 (July/June) was posted at 9.75 billion birr.
Meles said: "We still have a deficit in the capital expenditure outlay which will be covered through grants, assistance and commerical loans from abroad."

Ethiopia's free market reforms has been hailed by donor nations since the present rulers drove former Marxist dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam from power in 1991 in an uprising which ended years of civil war. ($=6.308 Ethiopia Birr)
